read: Thursday's news was about regulatory and capital-markets plumbing rather than data. Reuters reports the FDA has quietly let Makary's Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) programme lapse, just as Heidi Overton's nomination heads to a HELP committee vote on 18 November with uncertain numbers. That takes some of the fast-review premium out of voucher-holder stories and leaves agency leadership unsettled heading into a Democratic House. BMS folding research into development under Massacesi, a day after Pfizer's Blackstone funding, is another big pharma reorganising around its LOE cliff. The tape was risk-off: XBI fell roughly 3% (Yahoo Finance, including after-hours) and the IPO window split. Windward (China-sourced long-acting TSLP antibody, Sanofi anchor) priced at its $17 midpoint, while Rezera pulled its $200m deal on the eve of its debut. Capital is still going to de-risked, often China-originated assets with pharma validation, and turning away cash-thin stories.

items.headline: FDA reportedly shelves the CNPV fast-review programme ahead of the Overton committee vote
items.detail: Six sources told Reuters that applications can still be filed but will not advance. No vouchers have been awarded since Makary left in May; 22 drugs received one and 12 have been approved, including Merck's Lipfendra and RevMed's Rasonque. FDA says pilot work continues. RBC sees incremental timeline risk for Compass's COMP360 but keeps an 85% PoS estimate. The HELP vote on Overton is set for 18 November, and Sara Brenner could return as acting commissioner in 2027. Voucher holders' timelines revert toward standard priority review.

items.headline: Bristol Myers Squibb merges research and development under CMO Cristian Massacesi; research chief Robert Plenge to leave
items.detail: The unified R&D organisation starts in early 2027, with Plenge advising through March 2027. BMS did not comment on layoffs or pipeline changes. Pfizer-partnered Eliquis ($14.4bn in 2025) and Opdivo ($10bn) make up roughly half of $48.2bn revenue ahead of LOE, and BMO recently questioned the replacement assets (Cobenfy, milvexian with J&J, admilparant). Expect sharper portfolio pruning and BD.

items.headline: Kyverna completes its BLA for miv-cel in stiff person syndrome, requests priority review, and drops next-gen KYV-102
items.detail: If approved, this would be the first CAR-T for an autoimmune disease. One-year KYSA-8 data had patients staying off chronic immunotherapy with no high-grade CRS or ICANS. KYV-102 (same CD19 construct, whole-blood rapid manufacturing) is deprioritised to concentrate on neuro indications. This is the bellwether for autoimmune cell therapy.

items.headline: Vor Bio adds RemeGen's long-acting BAFF/APRIL successor RC298 to its ex-Greater China licence (about $56m upfront)
items.detail: Terms are $10m cash plus a pre-funded warrant for 2.3m shares (about $46m), and up to $300m in development milestones ($20m near term). RC298 is preclinical, with a China filing in 1H27. Runway is reaffirmed into early 2029. It is a lifecycle hedge for telitacicept (Phase 3 in gMG and Sjogren's), but the warrant shares create a resale overhang.

items.headline: Windward Bio prices its $175m Nasdaq IPO at $17 (midpoint), plus a $50m Sanofi private placement
items.detail: The deal is 10.29m shares for $225m combined proceeds, with trading from 13 November as WWB (about $1.0bn fully diluted at the midpoint). Lead asset WIN378 is a twice-yearly anti-TSLP antibody in-licensed from Kelun-Biotech and Harbour BioMed, in Phase 2/3 in asthma with Phase 2 data in 1H27. It is pitched against AstraZeneca/Amgen's monthly Tezspire.

items.headline: Rezera postpones its $200m IPO on the eve of its debut
items.detail: The IPO had been due to list on Friday. Terms were 16.7m shares at $11-13, with GSK indicating up to $25m. Per its S-1, cash without the IPO lasted only into January 2027. This is a clear sign the window is selective for cash-thin, Phase 3-ready stories.

items.headline: Vir prices a $150m follow-on at $10.00 after its ECLIPSE-1 Phase 3 win in hepatitis delta
items.detail: The offering is 15m shares (Leerink, Morgan Stanley, Evercore). ECLIPSE-1 (9 November) showed 44% of patients with undetectable HDV RNA plus normal ALT vs 0%, and 79% undetectable at week 48. The raise funds the push against Gilead's Hepcludex.

items.headline: Intellia presents more HAELO data for lonvo-z at ACAAI ahead of its 10 March 2027 PDUFA
items.detail: Benefit was consistent across HAE subgroups, with QoL improvements and launch preparation under way.

items.headline: Alumis reports new Phase 3 psoriasis data for oral TYK2 inhibitor envudeucitinib and will engage FDA on Phase 3 in SLE
items.detail: Alumis claims the highest reported week-48 PASI 100 among oral psoriasis therapies (a cross-trial claim), which puts it against BMS's Sotyktu. The SLE plan rests on the IFNGS-high subgroup of LUMUS.
